name: guilford-1781
title: Guilford Courthouse, March 1781: a WarMapper reconstruction
note: Written by pipeline/recon/guilford_1781.py. Every feature carries its source, method, confidence and dates.

properties.desc: The Great Salisbury road (New Garden road) across the battlefield
properties.basis: Picked by eye from Hatch's plate 1 and 2 (S138) and laid on the ground by the park boundary (pipeline/guilford_geo.py). West of the old park his road lies about 70 m south of today's New Garden Road; inside the park it runs near the trace the park keeps as the Historic New Garden Road.
properties.name: Great Salisbury road

properties.desc: The Reedy Fork road, north from the courthouse (Greene's line of retreat)
properties.basis: Picked by eye from Hatch's plate 1 (S138) and laid on the ground by the park boundary (pipeline/guilford_geo.py). Greene: "We retreated in good order to the Reedy-fork river" (S140).
properties.name: Reedy Fork road

properties.desc: The great road from New Garden Meeting House to Little Horsepen Creek
properties.basis: New Garden Road as the US Geological Survey drew it in 1951 (S146), before the suburbs, picked from the sheets reprojected to WGS 84; the last 300 m is a straight join to Hatch's road. A road of 1951 on the line of the great road (S138, p. 30; S144, p. 73), not a survey of 1781.
properties.name: Great Salisbury road

properties.desc: The great road south-west of New Garden, towards Deep River
properties.basis: The main road west from Guilford College on the 1951 sheet (S146). Which road of 1781 Cornwallis's column came by is not established here: Lee has the meeting house "near the point where the road from Deep River intersects the great road" (S141).
properties.name: road from Deep River

properties.desc: The cross road at New Garden (Ballinger Road)
properties.basis: Ballinger Road on the 1951 sheet (S146). The staff ride puts the last of the morning's fights at "the Ballenger and Great Salisbury Cross Roads" (S144, p. 74).
properties.name: cross road

properties.desc: Hunting Creek (Richland Creek today)
properties.basis: Picked by eye from Hatch's plate 1 (S138) and laid on the ground by the park boundary (pipeline/guilford_geo.py). The USGS draws Richland Creek about 70 m west of this line at the road.
properties.name: Hunting Creek

properties.desc: Little Horsepen Creek, where the British column crossed and deployed
properties.basis: Picked by eye from Hatch's plate 2 (S138) and laid on the ground by the park boundary (pipeline/guilford_geo.py).
properties.name: Little Horsepen Creek

properties.desc: Horsepen Creek, west of the battlefield
properties.basis: The stream of the 1951 sheet (S146).
properties.name: Horsepen Creek

properties.desc: The vale in front of the third line
properties.basis: Picked by eye from Hatch's plate 1 (S138) and laid on the ground by the park boundary (pipeline/guilford_geo.py). Hatch draws it as a vale; whether water ran in it in March 1781 is not said.
